summary: King Island Airport (KNS/YKII) is the primary aviation gateway to King Island, a remote and windswept landmass located in Bass Strait roughly halfway between Victoria and Tasmania. The airport is essential for connecting the island's small community to mainland Australia, with scheduled flights linking to Melbourne serving residents, tourists, and freight operations. Surrounded by open farmland and ocean views, it offers travelers their first taste of King Island's famously rugged, uncluttered landscape.
faqs:
Q: Which airlines operate from King Island Airport?
A: Sharp Airlines is the main carrier offering scheduled passenger services, primarily connecting King Island with Melbourne (Moorabbin Airport).

Q: How long is the flight from Melbourne to King Island?
A: The flight from Melbourne is approximately 50–60 minutes depending on routing and weather conditions over Bass Strait.

Q: When is the best time to fly to King Island?
A: The airport operates year-round, but summer (December–February) generally offers the most reliable flying weather, though Bass Strait crossings can be affected by wind at any time of year.

Q: Are there car rentals available at King Island Airport?
A: Yes, rental car operators and local hire services are available at the airport, though booking in advance is strongly recommended due to limited fleet size on the island.
transport_tips: Renting a car is practically essential on King Island, as there is no public transport network and distances between attractions can be significant. Airport to the main town of Currie takes roughly 10 minutes by car. Allow flexibility in your travel schedule, as Bass Strait weather can occasionally cause flight delays or cancellations.
local_tip: Pack a windproof jacket—King Island is famously exposed to strong westerly winds, and conditions at the airstrip and open countryside can change quickly even in mild weather.
